nodes.label: Add/Remove Color (Bitsy Tuxedo)
nodes.rationale: Lets drawings use more than two tones (e.g. highlight colors or richer backgrounds) without reusing tile/sprite roles; removal auto-remaps pixel indices so nothing points at a deleted color.

nodes.label: Explicit Drawing Tools (Brush/Eraser/Fill/Picker)
nodes.rationale: Replaces stock Bitsy's single click-to-toggle pixel behavior with four explicit tools (brush, eraser, fill, color picker) for more deliberate, discoverable editing.

nodes.label: Import Image into Drawing (Bitsy Tuxedo)
nodes.rationale: Lets creators start from a photo/image instead of hand-pixeling; always creates a new drawing (never overwrites) to avoid destructive surprises, and nearest-palette-matching with a confirmation prompt trades color fidelity for staying within the 64-color palette cap.

nodes.label: 512-Unit-Per-Pixel Em Convention
nodes.rationale: The ttx_to_bitsyfont.js script requires every visual pixel to map to a multiple of 512 font units (e.g. an 8px-high font needs a 4096-unit em) and glyphs positioned above the underline, so font designers must transform glyphs in FontStruct (moving them in multiples of 512 units per pixel) to satisfy the converter's assumptions.

nodes.label: Audio Import (Bitsy Tuxedo)
nodes.rationale: Lets creators preview an imported audio track as room music while composing; intentionally not exported since the engine's native music format and export pipeline only understand composed Tunes, not arbitrary audio files, so imported audio is editor-preview-only and stored in browser localStorage rather than the save file.

nodes.label: Music Panel (Bitsy Tuxedo merge)
nodes.rationale: Stock Bitsy had separate tune/blip toolbar toggles; Tuxedo merges them into one Music panel with tabs plus an added Audio tab, simplifying the toolbar to a single music toggle.

nodes.label: Brazilian Portuguese (pt-BR) Localization
nodes.rationale: Added as a distinct language entry from the pre-existing European Portuguese (pt) translation, since the dialects differ.

nodes.label: Theme Panel (Bitsy Tuxedo)
nodes.rationale: Purely a personal editor-display preference (dark mode, editing/playing tints) stored in localStorage per browser, kept separate from game data since it affects only the editor UI, not the exported game; distinct playing/editing tints make the current mode visually obvious at a glance.
